findings.title: Unauthenticated prototype pollution via SOAP `id` attribute in WSDL.xmlToObject (MultiRef table keyed by attacker-controlled ids)
findings.why_real: lib/wsdl.js:1193 declares `var refs = {}`. In p.onopentag (lib/wsdl.js:1251-1254) the attacker-controlled `id` attribute is used as a key: `if (!refs[id]) refs[id] = {...}`; for id="__proto__" refs[id] is Object.prototype (truthy) so no entry is created. In p.onclosetag (lib/wsdl.js:1319-1320) `refs[cur.id].obj = obj` then executes `Object.prototype.obj = <attacker-parsed element>`, adding an enumerable property to every object in the process. Same for id="constructor" (writes Object.obj), id="hasOwnProperty" etc. Reachability: Server._process (lib/server.js:149) calls wsdl.xmlToObject(input) on the raw POST body BEFORE the optional authenticate() hook (lib/server.js:157), so any unauthenticated POST to the SOAP path triggers it; the client (lib/client.js:230) parses untrusted server responses through the same function. Impact: after pollution, every for-in in the process enumerates `obj`; Server._process's `for (name in services)` (lib/server.js:175-197, services is a plain {} per lib/wsdl.js:336) then treats the attacker object as a service/port and throws on url.parse / binding lookup for every subsequent request, a persistent DoS until restart, plus process-wide prototype pollution of third-party code. Fix: `refs = Object.create(null)` so no inherited name can be reached; all uses of refs (bracket read/write, for-in) are valid on a null-prototype object.

pr_title: [Micro Security Scanning - HIGH PRIORITY] security: prevent prototype pollution via SOAP id attributes in xmlToObject
pr_body:
## Finding (HIGH, CWE-1321)

`WSDL.prototype.xmlToObject` (lib/wsdl.js) keeps a MultiRef lookup table `refs = {}` keyed by the `id` / `href` attribute values of the incoming SOAP XML. Those values are attacker-controlled. For `id="__proto__"`, `refs[id]` resolves to `Object.prototype` (truthy, so no entry is created) and the close-tag handler then runs `refs[cur.id].obj = obj`, i.e. **`Object.prototype.obj = <attacker object>`**. `id="constructor"`, `id="hasOwnProperty"` etc. likewise write onto shared built-ins.

**Reachability:** `Server._process` (lib/server.js:149) parses the raw POST body with `xmlToObject` *before* the optional `authenticate()` hook (line 157), so a single unauthenticated POST to the SOAP endpoint triggers it. The client (lib/client.js:230) parses untrusted server responses through the same code.

**Impact:** the polluted property is enumerable, so every `for...in` in the process now sees `obj`. In `Server._process` the `for (name in services)` loop (lib/server.js:175-197; `services` is a plain `{}`) then treats the attacker's element as a service/port and throws on `url.parse(port.location)` or the binding lookup for **every subsequent request**, a persistent denial of service until restart, in addition to process-wide prototype pollution affecting unrelated code.

## Fix

`lib/wsdl.js`: `var refs = Object.create(null)` so the table has no inherited names at all. Every use of `refs` is bracket read/write or `for...in`, all valid on a prototype-less object (ES5, Node >= 0.8 per package.json engines). No signature or control-flow change.

`test/server-test.js`: regression test posts a request with `<tickerSymbol id="__proto__">` to the stockquote server and asserts `Object.prototype` has no `obj` property afterwards.

## Adjacency

| Site | Status |
|---|---|
| lib/wsdl.js xmlToObject `href` handling (`refs[id].hrefs`) | Same table; covered by this fix |
| lib/wsdl.js xmlToObject `topObject[name] = obj` (close tag) | `__proto__` element names only re-parent the *local* parsed object; no global write. Unchanged (see residual) |
| lib/wsdl.js xmlToObject `messages[...]` / `portType.methods[...]` lookups | Read-only; inherited names throw TypeError which the server catches. The write at line 1238 is unreachable for inherited names. Unchanged |
| lib/client.js:230 (client parses untrusted responses) | Fixed by the same change |
| lib/wsdl.js `_parse` (WSDL document parsing) | Input is operator-supplied WSDL, not request data. Unchanged |
| CI | No GitHub Actions workflows in this repo (only legacy .travis.yml); no PR-triggered credentialed jobs |

## Logged, not fixed (MEDIUM/LOW)

- CWE-209: lib/server.js:131-134 writes `err.stack` to the HTTP response (e.g. unknown operation name causes a TypeError at lib/server.js:293).
- CWE-116: lib/server.js:100 reflects the request Content-Type header into the response unvalidated.
- LOW: lib/security/WSSecurity.js interpolates operator-configured credentials into XML without escaping.

## Residual exposure

- Element *names* such as `<__proto__>` inside the Body still set the prototype of the local parsed object (lib/wsdl.js close-tag handler). This does not write to any shared object, and an attacker can supply the same properties directly as elements, so no privilege change results. Handlers that rely on `key in args` semantics should be aware. Not changed to avoid altering parse behaviour for existing callers.
- Parsing still happens before `authenticate()`; unknown or inherited operation names produce a caught TypeError whose stack is returned to the caller (the logged CWE-209 item).
- No local toolchain: `npm install` and `node` execution were not permitted in this environment, so the change was verified by inspection only (one-token change on a local dictionary declaration; every `refs` access is bracket or for-in). **CI is the first real build/test run for this change.**
